Former chief minister of Jammu and Kashmir and President of Jammu and Kashmir National Conference on Thursday said the government’s belief that terrorism has ended was a misconception.“I regret that those who shout every day in Delhi that terrorism has ended…I want to remind them that terrorism is still present, and ways must be found to eliminate this terrorism,” Abdullah said.Abdullah’s remarks come a day after three CRPF personnel were injured in a terrorist gunfire in Kashmir’s Kulgam.Abdullah stated that terrorism would never succeed in the valley."If they (terrorists) think that by doing this (such attacks) they will swallow Kashmir, they should get out of this misconception.”Previously Abdullah had asked people not to be intimidated by terrorism. Article Title: Made-in-India 5G Radio Moves Closer To Market, Bulk Supplies Expected In 2027
Article Text:
Prof Kiran Kumar Kuchi, IIT Hyderabad; Prof Debabrata Das, Director, IIIT-Bangalore and Sridhar Pillalamarri, CEO, IIITB COMET Foundation (L-R), showcasing Made-in-India 5G and 5G-Advanced technology.

Bengaluru: A Made-in-India 5G radio has taken a step towards commercial deployment, with deep-tech company WiSig Networks opening commercial orders for the technology. Bulk supplies are expected to begin in 2027.The development is significant for India’s efforts to reduce dependence on imported telecom equipment and build capabilities in advanced wireless communication. The technology, which also has applications in 5G-Advanced networks, emerged from research led by Prof Kiran Kuchi at IIT Hyderabad, with support from IIITB COMET Foundation, Bengaluru, under the Department of Science and Technology’s National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems (NM-ICPS).The 5G radio uses multiple antennas working together to transmit and receive several signals simultaneously, a technique that helps improve network capacity, performance and coverage. Such capabilities are increasingly important as mobile data consumption rises and networks need to handle more connected devices and higher data traffic.The research was licensed to WiSig Networks, a deep-tech company founded at IIT Hyderabad.The company first showcased the radio at the Mobile World Congress in Barcelona in March 2026 and subsequently opened commercial orders at the India Mobile Congress in New Delhi in October.Prof. Debabrata Das, chairman of the governing body of IIITB COMET Foundation and director of IIIT-Bangalore, said the development demonstrated how academic research could progress towards commercial products.“This is precisely the kind of outcome that research funding should aim to achieve. It is encouraging to see research undertaken at an academic institution, with support from IIITB COMET Foundation, progress towards a product that has the potential for commercial deployment,” he said, underlining the importance of academia-industry collaboration in building indigenous capabilities in emerging technologies.Sridhar Pillalamarri, CEO of IIITB COMET Foundation, said: “The real value of research is also reflected in its ability to address practical needs.” He said the development showed how research support, technology transfer and industry participation could bring indigenous innovations closer to the market.The Foundation, established at IIIT-Bangalore under the NM-ICPS programme, supports research and technology development in advanced communication systems, including indigenous solutions for 5G and next-generation networks.The opening of commercial orders marks an important stage in the development of the technology, although large-scale supplies are yet to begin. Its commercial deployment will be an indicator of how effectively Indian research and industry can work together to build and take advanced telecommunications products to market.
Article Summary: WiSig Networks opens commercial orders for the technology. Bulk supplies are expected to begin in 2027. Development is significant for India’s efforts to reduce dependence on imported telecom equipment and build capabilities in advanced wireless communication. Technology emerged from research led by Prof Kiran Kuchi at IIT Hyderabad.

NEW DELHI: The government is planning to convene a special session of Parliament to secure the passage of a Constitution amendment bill linked to the implementation of women's reservation, PTI reported.According to the report, the BJP-led Centre is confident of securing 15 to 18 votes more than the 361 required to achieve a two-thirds majority and pass the proposed legislation. However, the dates and duration of the proposed special session remain unclear.The possibility of convening Parliament at short notice remains open, as the Monsoon Session, during which both Houses were adjourned sine die (indefinitely) on August 13, has yet to be prorogued. The session has now remained unprorogued for 91 days, surpassing the previous record of 87 days set in 2008.While an extended sitting of an existing session requires a minimum notice of two days, convening a fresh session requires at least 14 days' notice.The government's decision to keep the Monsoon Session unprorogued has consequently triggered speculation about the possibility of an extended sitting or a special session to consider the proposed amendment.The Constitution does not specify any timeframe within which a House must be prorogued after being adjourned sine die. Nor does keeping a session in continuation without formally proroguing it for an extended period, by itself, constitute any constitutional or procedural impropriety.The proposed constitutional amendment seeks to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from the existing 543 seats to a maximum of 850 through delimitation, paving the way for the implementation of 33% reservation for women in Parliament and state legislative assemblies.The move follows the failure of a similar Constitution amendment bill to secure the required majority in the Lok Sabha during a special sitting of the Budget Session on April 17.The government is proposing a 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats for every state to address concerns raised by southern states, as it seeks to implement the women's reservation law before the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.A fresh draft, which builds on the earlier bill, is understood to propose retaining the existing proportion of seats among states based on the 1971 Census.However, this is among several proposals under consideration, and no final decision has been taken, according to government sources.
Article Summary: The Centre is reportedly confident of securing 15-18 more votes than the 361 required to achieve a two-thirds majority. The dates and duration of the proposed special session remain unclear. The possibility of convening Parliament at short notice remains open, as the Monsoon Session has yet to be prorogued.

Article Title: 'Sad day for democracy': Bombay HC warns against criminalising constitutional right to protest
Article Text:
Bombay HC said criminal prosecutions should not be initiated to stifle agitations that form part of the democratic process, provided protesters do not resort to violence or damage public or private property.

NEW DELHI: The Bombay high court has quashed an FIR and chargesheet against a man booked for participating in a protest over poor road conditions in Maharashtra 's Chandrapur district, observing that it would be a "sad day for democracy" if criminal prosecutions were used to suppress peaceful agitations. The court said people have a constitutional right to protest as long as they do not resort to violence, take the law into their own hands or damage public or private property.Justice MW Chandwani of the high court's Nagpur bench made the observations in an order passed on October 29. A copy of the order was made available later.The case relates to an agitation held in January this year in Nandgaon village against the poor condition of a road. The protest followed an accident involving a vehicle on the damaged road. Residents had demanded action against the road contractor and officials of the Public Works Department.Nishkarsh Nimgade, a resident of Chandrapur district, was booked for participating in the agitation. The police alleged that the protesters had blocked the road by forming an unlawful assembly.Nimgade subsequently approached the High Court, seeking to quash the FIR and chargesheet filed against him.Allowing his petition, the court said Article 19(1)(b) of the Constitution guarantees citizens the right to assemble peacefully and without arms.It observed that while reasonable restrictions could be imposed on the exercise of this fundamental right, vague charges must not be used to dilute or suppress it."The lines between the constitutional right to protest and the unleashing of penal prosecutions cannot be allowed to be blurred. If this mindset gains traction, it would be a sad day for democracy," the HC remarked.The court further said criminal prosecutions should not be initiated to stifle agitations that form part of the democratic process, provided protesters do not resort to violence or damage public or private property.Describing the prosecution of Nimgade as an abuse of the legal process, the High Court quashed the FIR and chargesheet against him.
Article Summary: Bombay HC said criminal prosecutions should not be initiated to stifle agitations that form part of the democratic process. The court said people have a constitutional right to protest as long as they do not resort to violence, take the law into their own hands or damage public or private property.

NEW DELHI: The National Testing Agency (NTA) is planning a permanent pool of independent examination observers, including retired armed forces and paramilitary personnel and retired government officers, as part of efforts to strengthen examination security following the NEET-UG paper leak controversy.The observer's role is separate from and in addition to that of the city coordinator and centre superintendent, with a direct reporting line to the NTA."To meet the requirement in a timely and reliable manner across an annual examination cycle, NTA proposes to build and maintain a standing, pre-verified pool of empanelled Observers, drawn from retired and serving academic and administrative staff of government institutions," the EOI document said.The agency has invited applications under three categories: retired Central and state government officers; retired armed forces and paramilitary personnel; and retired or serving teachers and professors from government schools, colleges and universities.For examination centres located outside India, the NTA will ordinarily empanel observers from among Indian nationals residing in the same city.Separately, the NTA has invited institutions and organisations that own, operate or have legally enforceable use-rights over suitable facilities to apply for empanelment as examination centres.For computer-based tests (CBT), applicants are required to have 285 fully functional computer workstations, including buffer capacity, per shift.For pen-and-paper tests (PPT), a minimum of 250 candidate seats, including buffer capacity, per shift is required.CBT centres must have at least four separate computer labs or halls, each with 30 workstations. For PPT examinations, centres must have at least six separate halls accommodating 40 candidates each, or equivalent configurations.The initiatives come amid efforts to overhaul the national examination system following the NEET-UG paper leak controversy, which triggered nationwide student protests and raised questions about the security and integrity of competitive examinations.
Article Summary: The National Testing Agency is planning a permanent pool of independent examination observers. The observer's role is separate from and in addition to that of the city coordinator and centre superintendent. The initiatives come amid efforts to overhaul the national examination system following the NEET-UG paper leak controversy.

NEW DELHI: National Conference president Farooq Abdullah on Thursday advocated dialogue between India and Pakistan , saying meaningful engagement between New Delhi and Islamabad must begin without waiting for hostilities to end.Talking to reporters, Abdullah asserted that bullets and military confrontation cannot resolve political disputes."Ab aap intezaar karenge, jab tak aap sabki goliyan band ho jayengi, tab tak raat ho jayegi (If you keep waiting for everyone to stop firing, it will be too late by the time the guns fall silent)," Abdullah said."I have always told Pakistan to stop terrorism. Nothing can be achieved through terrorism. The process of dialogue must begin because only through talks can a way forward be found," he added.The former Jammu and Kashmir chief minister also called for the revival of SAARC, saying regional countries must come together to resolve their differences and work towards collective progress."India is the largest country in the region, and Indira Gandhi had shown the way for India to maintain cordial and sympathetic relations with neighbouring countries.We must revive SAARC so that all of us can sit together, resolve our disputes and work towards progress and development," he said.Reacting to the recent twin terror attacks in Kulgam and Kishtwar districts, which claimed the lives of two Special Police Officers (SPOs) and left three CRPF personnel injured within two days, Abdullah asserted that those harbouring ambitions of taking Kashmir must abandon such notions. He also said that terrorism would never succeed in its designs.However, he expressed concern over claims in Delhi that terrorism had ended in Jammu and Kashmir, maintaining that the recent incidents indicated that the threat persisted and that concrete measures were needed to eliminate it."I have already said such incidents are still happening. One never knows where the next attack might take place," he said.This comes days after Abdullah courted criticism for his remarks that Pakistan's repeated efforts to raise the Kashmir issue internationally were putting pressure on India.He alleged that the Centre's intentions towards Jammu and Kashmir were not good and urged people to stand up for their rights.“What can you expect from Delhi? NEW DELHI: Security agencies have intensified their manhunt for Mohammad Lateef Bhat, one of four active terrorists featured on a recently released wanted poster by Jammu and Kashmir Police, following his identification as a suspect in Wednesday’s attack on CRPF personnel in Kulgam.Bhat, a resident of Khrewan Chadder in Kulgam, is considered one of the few remaining local terrorists active in the valley. He is affiliated with the Kashmir Revolutionary Army (KRA), a proxy group floated by Pak-based Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) to conceal its direct involvement.Operating across South Kashmir, particularly in the Kulgam, Shopian, and Anantnag districts, Bhat is known to exercise influence over local over ground worker (OGW) networks.Investigating agencies suspect Bhat’s involvement in several recent terror strikes in the region. These include the July 22 fatal shooting of J&K Police Head Constable Aashiq Hussain in Anantnag and the July 31 targeted killing of two migrant workers from Chhattisgarh, Deepak and Bhupendra, in Kulgam.Security forces noted that Bhat operates differently from standard modules. “Known to be possessing an AK-47, he executes swift strikes either alone or in small groups before immediately blending into the local population,” said a source.In July 2026, Bhat was trapped alongside top LeT commander Zakir Ganie during a security force siege on a house in Shopian. While Ganie was neutralised in the encounter, Bhat is learnt to have managed to break through the cordon and escape, evading a massive follow-up search operation.While law enforcement agencies state that the other three individuals listed on the wanted poster— Bilal Ahmad Mir, Abid Qayoom Lone, and Mohammad Umar Mir — are currently operating from across the border in Pakistan-occupied Jammu & Kashmir (PoJK), Bhat remains the sole local operative actively grounded in South Kashmir.Authorities had last week issued a public appeal for information on the whereabouts of the four suspects, promising strict confidentiality and a cash reward. Inputs can be shared directly with security agencies through designated helplines, they had said.

Article Title: India simplifies visa rules: Categories cut to 9 from 13, application fields reduced by up to 70%
Article Text:
The rationalisation of visitor visa, earlier called tourist visa, allows flexibility for short and long stays.

NEW DELHI: Having simplified its visa regime by cutting the total visa categories to 9 from 13 and sub-categories to 23 from 49 and also reducing the information sought from foreign applicants across all 23 sub-categories, the ministry of home affairs (MHA) will be MHA updating its IT systems by year-end, to grant visas per new rationalisation."The step aims at making it (visa regime) more compact, coherent and responsive to the requirements of foreign nationals visiting India," the home ministry said in a statement on Wednesday. As part of the revamp, the main visa categories were first cut on 22 to 13 and sub-categories to 49 from 63 in October last year, and further to 9 and 23 respectively on August 27 this year. This simplification was done after studying the visa system followed by the developed countries as well as the global standards."The consolidation of similar purposes of travel is aimed at providing greater clarity and ease in identifying the appropriate visa category while facilitating legitimate foreign arrivals," said a ministry spokesperson.Currently electronic visa or e visa is processed by electronic travel authorization under 13 sub categories. The e-visa facility is available to nationals of 172 countries.The MHA has also made visa application simpler, cutting the fields/columns by upto 70% across all 23 sub-categories of visas."The initiative aims to significantly reduce the information required from foreign nationals, while retaining essential details necessary for visa processing. This will reduce time and effort required to complete the application and also enhance administrative efficiency by facilitating more focused scrutiny and processing of visa application," said MHA.The rationalisation of visitor visa, earlier called tourist visa, allows flexibility for short and long stays. The name visitor visa reflects a broader range of permitted purposes beyond conventional tourism. The category has been organised into two sub-categories, V-1 and V-2. V-1 covers short-term activities such as business meetings, medical consultations, wellness retreats, and short term courses. It is granted for 30 days with multiple entries. V2 is for longer-duration visits, with validity of 1, 5 or 10 years, as specified.The medical visa framework retains separate provisions for treatment under conventional and AYUSH systems. M-1 Visa covers medical treatment other than treatment under AYUSH systems, while M-3 Visa covers treatment under AYUSH systems. M-1 and M-3 Visas, including their e-Visa variants, will be granted for one year as a default option with multiple entries.This arrangement gives patients greater predictability when treatment involves multiple consultations, follow-up appointments or staged procedures.In the student visa category, S-1 covers school and college education while the S-2 is meant for PhD and research scholars in Indian universities.Business visas shall now also divided into B-1 and B-2. B-1 Visa covers long-term, licence-based business activities, including foreign nationals seeking to establish industrial or business ventures in India. B-2 Visa covers short-term, contract-based business activities, including Production Investment Business, conferences, sports, performative arts and films.A specific provision has also been made for foreign subject-matter specialists, engineers and technical personnel engaged by Indian companies. Such personnel may be granted a production investment business visa under the B-2 category through the e-Visa platform. This was earlier granted under e-B4 visa nomenclature."This differentiation gives businesses greater clarity when planning long-term investments as against short-term contractual assignments. The dedicated provision for technical specialists can facilitate timely deployment of expertise for setting up and operationalising industrial facilities, transferring technology, etc," as per MHA.The ministry said the changes in visa regime reduce overlap between visa categories and make the framework easier to navigate for visitors, patients, students, researchers, investors and business professionals. The rationalisation is intended to support legitimate travel, education, healthcare and economic engagement with India through clearer, purpose-based visa options, subject to applicable eligibility criteria and conditions.
Article Summary: Ministry of home affairs (MHA) will be MHA updating its IT systems by year-end, to grant visas per new rationalisation. The rationalisation of visitor visa, earlier called tourist visa, allows flexibility for short and long stays. The name visitor visa reflects a broader range of permitted purposes beyond conventional tourism.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday recalled how a group of journalists once informed him that he had become the chief minister of Gujarat, asking him to distribute sweets.Addressing journalists at the BJP headquarters, PM Modi said only a few senior party leaders were aware of the development when a group of journalists walked into his room and told him, “You are the CM of Gujarat now, mithai khilao. ”Recalling his journey with the media, PM Modi said he had witnessed its transformation from the days of press releases to the present era of Instagram reels. Article Title: Arvind Kejriwal, daughter Harshita get death threats from Bishnoi gang; Rs 7 crore demanded
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: On Christmas Day 1978, Sonia Gandhi carried a home-cooked lunch into Tihar Jail for her imprisoned mother-in-law, Indira Gandhi , and, at the former Prime Minister's request, enough extra for a young Australian woman she describes as the accomplice of serial killer Charles Sobhraj.The episode appears in Belonging: A Journey of Love, Sonia Gandhi's memoir, released on November 10. It is set in the week Indira Gandhi spent in Tihar after the Janata Party , the combined opposition formation, came to power in the elections that followed the Emergency. Sonia writes that she visited the jail daily during that period.Also Read| When Sonia Gandhi carried lunch to Tihar for Charles Sobhraj's accomplice Christmas, she recalls, had always been a special day in the household, especially for the children, even when Sanjay and Rajiv were little boys. "The celebration had no religious meaning for us, but it was a festive day when we exchanged gifts and decorated the house with colourful baubles and red poinsettias," she writes."But on this Christmas my mother-in-law was in jail. I felt that I had to do something special to keep our spirits up."A friend offered to send sliced ham with roast potatoes and a small Christmas pudding, while Sonia would prepare "a good soup and some vegetables".The plan soon had to expand."At my mother-in-law's request, the food had to be enough also for the three women who took turns guarding her and a young woman prisoner in her compound," Sonia writes. She identifies the prisoner as "an Australian girl, the accomplice of the dreaded Charles Sobraj, convicted for multiple murders of young tourists in Thailand, Nepal, and India"."My mother-in-law felt sorry for her," Sonia writes.Then came a hitch. "When it turned out that she didn't eat ham, we quickly had to change the menu and prepare a roast chicken instead."There was resistance from within the jail as well. The day before, Indira Gandhi had sent a note saying that "under no circumstances" should her daughter-in-law deliver lunch. Sonia was to have her Christmas meal with Rajiv and the children."I couldn't do it," she writes.She went to Tihar with the food, a book as a small gift, and cards from the children. "I rushed back rather late, but satisfied that I could celebrate with her briefly and also have lunch with Rajiv and the children," she recalls."As it happened, she was released the next day and came home."The passage offers a rare domestic glimpse into one of the most dramatic periods of modern Indian politics: a former prime minister in jail, her daughter-in-law shuttling between kitchen and cell, and a Christmas lunch stretched to include guards and a fellow prisoner linked to a notorious killer.

Article Title: SC: Indians married here can't get divorced abroad
Article Text:
SC: Indians married here can't get divorced abroad

Irretrievable breakdown of marriage no divorce ground in Indian law: SC

NEW DELHI: Taking advantage of liberal laws abroad to obtain a divorce for a wedding solemnised in India will not automatically lead to dissolution of the marriage under Indian law, Supreme Court has ruled.Viewing negatively the use in a foreign court of grounds for divorce which are not recognised in India, SC said a person who contracts a second marriage on that basis may face prosecution for bigamy as the first marriage continues to subsist under Indian law, reports Amit Anand Choudhary.With many men approaching a foreign court to get a divorce on the ground of irretrievable breakdown of marriage - despite the wife opposing the plea - and thereafter remarrying, SC said the person has to face proceedings even in a case where he had become a citizen of a foreign country. The top court said legal consequences stemm-ing from the subsisting marriage cannot be overridden by a subsequent change in a spouse's nationality.The bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar allowed criminal proceedings for bigamy against a man who remarried after getting a divorce order from a foreign court on the ground of irretrievable breakdown of marriage in proceedings opposed by the wife.The court said that irretrievable breakdown of marriage is not a ground for divorce in Indian law and, therefore, the divorce granted by the foreign court is not valid.“In our view, the foreign divorce decree was passed in contravention of the existing matrimonial law in India and on a ground that is not even recognised statutorily. This violates the legal threshold of Section 13 of the CPC, which every foreign decree has to pass through,” the SC bench said.The bench also said that if the foreign decree does not satisfy the requirements of Section 13 of the Civil Procedure Code, then the husband, relying on such a decree, cannot be permitted to contend that his first marriage stood dissolved in the eyes of matrimonial laws of India and, thus, escape the rigours of Section 494 of IPC (marrying again during lifetime of husband or wife).“Now, coming to the argument of the husband that since he was a British citizen when the second marriage with second wife was solemnised and since the second marriage took place outside India, keeping in view the mandate of Section 4 of the IPC, he cannot be held liable. We cannot accept this submission in the manner canvassed as the husband was married to first wife in India under Hindu rites, rituals and customs; thus, even if the second marriage took place outside India, the allegations under Section 494 of the IPC cannot be said to be diluted since enquiry for the offence of bigamy cannot be confined to the place of second marriage but must necessarily take into account the subsisting matrimonial relationship. ..” the bench said.The court, however, quashed criminal proceedings against the parents and second wife of the man.
Article Summary: Supreme Court rules that divorce for a wedding solemnised in India will not automatically lead to dissolution of the marriage under Indian law. A person who contracts a second marriage on that basis may face prosecution for bigamy as the first marriage continues to subsist.

Article Title: Sheikh Hasina, water and trade: Roadblocks in India-Bangladesh ties
Article Text:
The Sheikh Hasina question: At the heart of diplomatic tension

Sheikh Hasina's road back to Bangladesh

Shared rivers, competing interest

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe the extradition of Sheikh Hasina will ease tensions between India and Bangladesh? Yes, it will No, it won't 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

All about India-Bangladesh Ganga water-sharing treaty

The trade roadblock

India’s continued outreach to Bangladesh

Who is Dinesh Trivedi, India's high commissioner to Bangladesh

The road ahead for India-Bangladesh ties

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Over two years ago, student protests against the quota system in Bangladesh’s government jobs evolved into a nationwide uprising that brought down the government of then Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina , forcing her to flee to India. The political upheaval ushered in a period of considerable strain in bilateral relations with India, and New Delhi-Dhaka ties have since deteriorated significantly. This is reflected in the fact that Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, who assumed office in February, is yet to visit New Delhi, despite having travelled to other countries in the region.The tensions have also spilled over into negotiations on the future of the Ganga Water Sharing Treaty and bilateral trade. Political mistrust has complicated efforts to reach a consensus on water-sharing, while reciprocal trade restrictions have added to economic friction.These issues have emerged as significant roadblocks in bilateral ties. The challenge for New Delhi and Dhaka, therefore, is not merely to resolve disagreements but to ensure that political differences do not undermine the broader framework of bilateral cooperation.The departure of Sheikh Hasina from Bangladesh in August 2024 marked a turning point in bilateral ties. Her subsequent presence in India became a major source of disagreement between New Delhi and Dhaka.During her tenure, Sheikh Hasina had maintained close relations with successive governments in New Delhi, cooperating on issues such as counterterrorism, connectivity, transit and regional security. India, in turn, viewed her as an important partner in maintaining stability in its eastern neighbourhood.However, this fuelled perceptions among a significant section of the public in Bangladesh that India had prioritised its own strategic interests over broader democratic and political concerns in their country. This perception contributed to a growing anti-India sentiment and played a part in the political developments that eventually led to Sheikh Hasina’s ouster.Since then, both the Muhammad Yunus-led interim administration that succeeded Sheikh Hasina and the subsequent Bangladesh Nationalist Party government, elected in February, have repeatedly sought the former prime minister’s extradition to face the law for “crimes against humanity” linked to the July Uprising, as the movement is known as in Bangladesh. Meanwhile, India has maintained that the request is being examined through the established legal process.Also, Sheikh Hasina has already announced that she would return to Bangladesh in December, a timeline that is now drawing closer. If her return materialises, it could bring the extradition question to a close, although the legal and political issues surrounding her return may continue to test ties. A press conference she addressed on August 5, the second anniversary of her resignation, further complicated matters.According to Sreeradha Datta, Professor of International Affairs at OP Jindal Global University, the extradition impasse is not a roadblock in itself; rather, it is the manner in which the two sides have handled the issue that has become the stumbling block.“The roadblock is how the two sides deal with it. And the fact that the Bangladesh government laid down a condition like that (extradition) for a visit to occur is actually what has complicated the matter,” she said, referring to Tarique Rahman’s yet-to-take-place visit.Datta added that Rahman could have visited India and discussed the matter with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, but setting a precondition only complicated the issue further.Ultimately, how the Sheikh Hasina matter is handled will be an important test of New Delhi and Dhaka’s ability to manage political differences while keeping the broader relationship on track.While the extradition impasse represents a relatively recent political challenge, disagreements over river water-sharing have long been a feature of India-Bangladesh relations. Since they share 54 transboundary rivers, differences over the equitable distribution of water are natural.However, a formal water-sharing treaty exists only for the river known as the Ganga in India and the Padma in Bangladesh. Signed on December 12, 1996, the 30-year agreement is due to expire on December 12 this year. With the renewal deadline approaching, Dhaka has called for a new or revised, longer-term agreement that includes a “guarantee” clause to ensure an assured supply of water to Bangladesh, particularly during the dry season and periods of low river levels.Datta noted that water remains an emotive and sensitive issue for Bangladesh, adding that while a new 30-year agreement may or may not materialise, she hoped the two sides could reach an interim arrangement.“For Bangladesh, water is the most emotive and sensitive issue. … Even if we don't expect a long-term 30-year agreement, I hope there is an interim agreement because both are agro-based economies and Bangladesh’s dependence on the common rivers is far more,” she said.Beyond the Ganga/Padma, India and Bangladesh have also had longstanding disagreements over the sharing of Teesta waters. A deal came close to being finalised in 2011 but was blocked by then West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee, citing her state’s needs. Dhaka has been seeking a formal treaty to secure an adequate share of Teesta’s waters, particularly during the dry season, when declining flows affect irrigation and agricultural activities.With the BJP, which has been India’s governing party since 2014, now also governing West Bengal, there are hopes that the long-pending Teesta agreement may finally materialise.Nevertheless, against the backdrop of recent tensions, the unresolved water-sharing disputes remain another major irritant in India-Bangladesh ties.Despite strained ties, India remains Bangladesh’s third-largest trading partner. It briefly overtook the United States in February before Washington reclaimed the second spot, while China continues to be the largest trading partner by a distance.Yet, with both sides imposing trade restrictions, economic ties remain under strain, adding another layer of friction to an already tense relationship.For instance, in April 2025, Dhaka restricted the entry of Indian yarn through several land ports, citing concerns over its domestic textile industry. The same month, New Delhi withdrew the transshipment facility that had allowed Bangladeshi export cargo to pass through Indian territory en route to third countries. The following month, India further tightened import restrictions on several categories of Bangladeshi goods through land ports, including ready-made garments and certain processed products.The curbs were discussed during trade negotiations held in New Delhi last month, marking the first meeting of the bilateral joint working group after a prolonged gap. The Bangladeshi side reportedly called for a review of restrictions on the entry of goods through Indian land ports, while India sought the removal of curbs on its cotton yarn exports.Both sides also called for the removal of other trade restrictions imposed by the other.Despite continued engagement through bilateral talks, these differences remain unresolved, adding to the wider set of contentious issues straining ties between New Delhi and Dhaka.Likely anticipating Tarique Rahman's eventual rise to power, New Delhi began reaching out to him following his return to Bangladesh in December 2025, after a 17-year stay in the UK. External affairs minister S Jaishankar attended the funeral of former Bangladesh Prime Minister Khaleda Zia, Rahman’s mother, who passed away just days after her son’s return to the country. Later, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla and foreign secretary Vikram Misri represented India at Rahman’s swearing-in ceremony.Then, in April, former Union minister Dinesh Trivedi was appointed as India’s high commissioner to Bangladesh, marking a relatively rare instance of a political figure being chosen for a diplomatic posting.According to Sreeradha Datta, the move signals New Delhi’s seriousness about improving ties with Bangladesh and has, therefore, been well-received in Dhaka.“He (Trivedi) has been able to have a good outreach and he seems to have got along well with the Bangladeshis. His appointment has been well received and it probably conveyed to Bangladesh that the government was giving more attention and hoping that a political appointee would have greater ability to move things,” she said.Having been in the post for only six months, whether Trivedi can help bring about a broader reset in the relationship remains to be seen.India-Bangladesh relationship remains strained by a range of unresolved issues, extending beyond the impasse over Sheikh Hasina’s extradition to disputes over river-water sharing and trade. These include concerns over India’s alleged “forced push-ins” of suspected undocumented Bangladeshi immigrants, the alleged killings of Bangladeshi “civilians” by the Border Security Force at the India-Bangladesh border, and Dhaka’s pro-Pakistan tilt that began under the interim administration, among others.Yet, the relationship remains strategically important for both sides: Bangladesh is critical to India’s security interests, while Dhaka depends on New Delhi across several key sectors.Against this backdrop, Datta stressed that cooperation between New Delhi and Dhaka is in the interest of both, as well as the wider region.“India and Bangladesh have to work together for their own benefit. For the last two years, we've seen them not work with each other (but) it makes greater sense for not only the bilateral partners, but also for the region when India and Bangladesh work together,” she said.Ultimately, despite the many unresolved roadblocks, India and Bangladesh have little choice but to find a way to work together because of geography and shared strategic interests. The question is how soon both sides can move beyond the current strains.
Article Summary: Sheikh Hasina's extradition to India is at the heart of diplomatic tension. Tensions have spilled over into negotiations on the future of the Ganga Water Sharing Treaty and bilateral trade. Political mistrust has complicated efforts to reach a consensus on water-sharing. reciprocal trade restrictions have added to economic friction.

Article Title: Confident of trade pact ahead of PM Modi's trip: Canada envoy

As India and Canada hold the 6th round of trade negotiations this week, Canada's high commissioner to India Christopher Cooter has said Ottawa is confident of finalising the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) ahead of PM Narendra Modi's visit to Canada next month.While the agreement will still have to be ratified, the announcement about successful conclusion of the negotiations during Modi's Dec 11-12 visit will mark a milestone in the relationship, capping the dramatic turnaround in India-Canada ties under Canadian PM Mark Carney and Modi in the past 18 months."The actual ratification would take some time because we have provincial governments that are involved as well. But I think we can be pretty confident that the final text will be there," said Cooter in an interaction with TOI editors."We're hopeful about our ratification process. The 6th round of talks is coming up. I'm pretty confident that we're getting close, so we'll keep our fingers crossed. We're also looking at some subsidiary agreements that would facilitate business travel," added Cooter. He also said many other big-ticket announcements were expected from the visit including in space.Cooter also addressed public anxiety over international student policies of Canada, home to roughly 300,000 Indian students. He clarified that official caps were targeted at fraudulent institutions rather than legitimate Indian applicants."People said, 'Oh my God, Canada's not open'. This was a misperception. In fact, the caps are nowhere near being met. This is probably the best time ever, if you're a prospective Indian student. Of course there were some abuses. There were these fly-by-night colleges. They weren't about education as much as getting PR. So, we've got to clean that up," said Cooter.Cooter also said the progress witnessed in the ties since Carney assumed office had moved "far beyond a reset". He said the recovery was initially fragile, but gained unprecedented momentum following bilateral engagements between the leaders."It's not a reset. It is far beyond a reset. When I arrived here in Sept last year, it was a tentative approach. None of us knew what was going to happen next. Is this going to be a slow march? Are we going to take a step back? Very fragile at the beginning. But it didn't happen that way. When foreign minister Anita Anand was here last month, we called on your PM and he described it as the fastest acceleration in the relationship," said Cooter.
Article Summary: Canada's high commissioner to India Christopher Cooter said Ottawa is confident of finalising the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) ahead of PM Narendra Modi's visit to Canada next month. NEW DELHI: All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen ( AIMIM ) chief Asaduddin Owaisi and Azad Samaj Party (Kanshiram) president Chandrashekhar Azad are likely to announce an alliance for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections at a joint press conference in Lucknow on Thursday, November 12.The proposed tie-up could mark an attempt by the two parties to build a political front outside the BJP-led NDA and the Samajwadi Party-Congress alliance. Both parties are looking to consolidate support among Dalit and minority voters, who together account for nearly 41 per cent of Uttar Pradesh's electorate, according to the figures cited by party leaders.AIMIM spokesperson Shadab Chauhan confirmed that the two parties would join hands, but said details of the agreement would be made public at the press conference, news agency PTI reported.The event is expected to be held at a hotel in Gomtinagar and will be addressed by Owaisi and leaders of the Bhim Army.Both leaders have reached Lucknow ahead of the announcement. He said further details would be shared on Thursday.The parties have not yet disclosed how many of the state's 403 assembly seats they intend to contest.It is also unclear whether other smaller parties will join the proposed front.The development follows Owaisi's unsuccessful attempt to secure a place in the INDIA bloc's seat-sharing arrangement in Uttar Pradesh. The AIMIM chief had set an October 2 deadline for the Samajwadi Party and Congress to respond to his offer, but neither party agreed to include him in the alliance.While AIMIM has a limited electoral footprint in Uttar Pradesh, Owaisi has influence among sections of the minority community. Azad, the Nagina MP, has been seeking to expand his support among young Dalit voters. Their proposed partnership could therefore add another political equation to the contest, as the BJP looks to retain power for a third consecutive term and the opposition seeks to challenge it.

Article Title: Complete data could've raised average Diwali pollution level in Delhi by 49%
Article Text:
Complete data could've raised avg Diwali pollution level 49%

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Missing PM2.5 data from monitoring stations could have raised the city's average pollution level by 49% on Diwali, according to an analysis by Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA).Had the missing readings been recorded at 1,000 micrograms per cubic metre (g/m³), the city's average PM2.5 level would have increased from 269 to 400(g/m³), it revealed. The daily national ambient air quality standard for PM2.5 is 60 g/m³ and WHO's safe guideline is 15 g/m³.The analysis was done a day after Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) said its stations' analysers were calibrated to measure particulate matter concentrations only up to 1,000g/m³ and could not display readings beyond it on Diwali night for several hours.Nor were these readings considered for calculating the average AQI, it said.CREA said if 400g/m³ had been considered, city's AQI on Monday would have risen from 344 (very poor) to near severe. AQI is calculated based on 8 pollutants, including PM2.5.TOI reported Tuesday that CPCB had stopped giving data on particulate matter at the peak of Diwali night pollution for several hours after particulate matter levels at air quality monitoring stations surpassed 1,000g/m³.However, Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC), which operates 43 of the total 60 stations, gave readings on Diwali night that crossed 1,000g/m³. At least at 11 locations, the hourly PM2.5 concentration was above 2,000g/m³. In four, it was above 3,000.CPCB compiles data from all 60 stations and releases the AQI. One station has been defunct for the past few months.The latest analysis examined hourly PM2.5 data from 59 monitoring stations between 4pm on Nov 8 and 4pm on Nov 9, corresponding to the 24-hour averaging period used for CPCB's 4pm AQI bulletin on Nov 9. It analysed 1,416 hours (24 hours x 59 stations).It found that 255 of the 1,416 expected station-hour observations or 18% were missing. CREA conducted a sensitivity analysis by assigning them a value of 1,000g/m³, the upper measurement limit cited by CPCB for particulate matter. Under this scenario, the pooled average PM2.5 concentration across the expected observations increased from 269g/m³ to 400g/m³, a rise of 49%."The peak PM2.5 levels of Delhi was 584 g/m³ at 1am on Nov 9 when there was missing data. However, after replacing the missing data with 1,000 g/m³, the peak PM2.5 concentration was 825 g/m³ at 2am and 824 g/m³ at 3am," said CREA.It clarified that the sensitivity analysis does not establish that all 255 missing observations were caused by PM2.5 concentrations exceeding 1,000g/m³. Assigning the upper measurement limit to these observations was only an illustrative exercise to understand how the reported average could change under such a scenario.TOI reported Tuesday that hourly PM2.5 levels at Mundka touched 3,744g/m³ at 2am Monday, according to DPCC's data. However, CPCB did not share Mundka's PM2.5 readings from 12 midnight to 4 am.
Article Summary: Missing PM2.5 data from monitoring stations could have raised the city's average pollution level by 49% on Diwali. Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) said its stations' analysers were calibrated to measure particulate matter only up to 1,000g/m³.

Article Title: Centre simplifies visa regime: Paperwork cut by 70%, categories reduced from 13 to 9
Article Text:

Student visa category

reorganised

NEW DELHI: The Centre has simplified India's visa regime, reducing the number of main visa categories from 13 to nine and sub-categories from 49 to 23, in a move aimed at making travel, education and medical treatment in the country easier for foreign nationals.The ministry of home affairs (MHA), in a press release on Wednesday, said the number of fields to be filled in visa application forms across all 23 sub-categories has been reduced by 65-70%, making the process easier, faster and more applicant-friendly.This follows an earlier rationalisation in October 2025, when the number of main visa categories was reduced from 22 to 13 and sub-categories from 63 to 49.As part of the changes, the Student Visa category has been consolidated into two broad sub-categories — S-1 and S-2.The S-1 Visa covers school, graduate and post-graduate education, while the S-2 Visa covers PhD scholars and research students in Indian universities, visiting faculty, foreign research students visiting India, scientific and anthropological expeditions, internships and exchange programmes, among other specified academic activities.Foreign students enrolled in Indian educational institutions through the Study in India portal may be granted an e-S1 Visa for up to five years or for the duration of their academic course, whichever is shorter.The visa will allow multiple entries.Under the revised framework, the erstwhile Tourist Visa has been renamed the Visitor Visa. Provisions relating to medical, student and business visas have also been reorganised.The MHA is updating its information technology systems to implement the revised framework, with visas under the new system expected to be issued by the end of 2026.
Article Summary: The number of main visa categories has been reduced from 13 to nine. The Student Visa category has been consolidated into two broad sub-categories. The erstwhile Tourist Visa has been renamed the Visitor Visa. Provisions relating to medical, student and business visas have been reorganised.

Article Title: Green energy push helped India save $100bn over last 15 yrs: IEA
Article Text:
Green energy push helped India save $100bn over last 15 yrs: IEA

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Expansion of renewable energy (RE) capacity over the past 15 years helped India save more than $100 billion in coal and natural gas import costs, the International Energy Agency (IEA) has said in a recent report.With 300GW of RE capacity, India has emerged as the world's second-fastest-growing renewables market, strengthening its energy security, the report said. India added 168GW of solar and 38GW of wind capacity between March 2014 and Sept 2026, while installed bioenergy capacity reached nearly 12GW. With RE capacity expected to reach 530GW by 2030, IEA estimated that cumulative savings on coal and natural gas imports could reach $240 billion by 2030, assuming international fuel prices remain broadly at their 2024-25 average levels. Annual savings are projected to reach around $35 billion by then, exceeding India's entire spending on non-coking coal and natural gas imports in FY25.The India Renewable Energy Market Report 2026 estimated that without the solar PV, wind and bioenergy capacity added since 2010, India's coal imports in 2025 would have been around 110 million tonnes higher."India's experience shows how consistent policies can help drive down renewable energy costs and attract investment, offering valuable lessons for other emerging economies," said IEA executive director Fatih Birol.India achieved its target of sourcing 50% of installed electricity capacity from non-fossil fuel sources in 2025, five years ahead of schedule.IEA said the growth extended beyond large plants, supported by rooftop solar installations, corporate RE procurement and expansion of domestic manufacturing facilities. It specifically highlighted the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana for accelerating rooftop solar installations and PM-KUSUM for supporting solar-powered irrigation pumps and farm feeders.
Article Summary: Green energy push helped India save $100bn over last 15 yrs: IEA. With 300GW of RE capacity, India has emerged as the world's second-fastest-growing renewables market. India added 168GW of solar and 38GW of wind capacity between March 2014 and Sept 2026.

Article Title: 'Misleading': Election Commission rejects claims of vote-count discrepancies in 2024 polls
Article Text:
The poll body shared constituency-wise details to clarify the figures.

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission of India (ECI) on Wednesday rejected social media claims of discrepancies between the number of votes polled and votes counted in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections and state assembly polls describing the allegations as "misleading. "In a post on X, the poll body shared screenshots of claims concerning constituencies in Maharashtra, Haryana and Jammu and Kashmir, along with constituency-wise data to clarify the figures."This is with reference to a social media post claiming inconsistencies in the number of votes polled and votes counted in the General Elections to the Lok Sabha, 2024 and General Elections to Legislative Assemblies of States held in 2024," the ECI said in a statement.The Commission said it publishes details of electors, votes polled through electronic voting machines (EVMs), postal ballots and total votes cast in its statistical reports and index cards. These records are available on its website.It also questioned the reference to "internal records" in the claims, saying the post had named certain constituencies and alleged that the ECI had counted zero votes there, but had not specified which records it was relying on.The Commission said Form 17C is the sole statutory account of votes cast at a polling station. It is prepared by the presiding officer at the close of polling.Copies of Part-I of Form 17C are given to polling agents appointed by candidates who are present at the polling station when voting concludes, the ECI said.On counting day, candidates' counting agents match the number of votes polled, recorded in Part-I of Form 17C, with the total number of votes counted, recorded in Part-II of the form.The Commission reiterated that all election-related data, including the number of votes polled and counted, had been made available through its statistical reports and index cards.It said the claims of discrepancies in the constituencies cited in the report were misleading and shared constituency-wise details to clarify the figures.
Article Summary: The Election Commission of India (ECI) rejected social media claims of discrepancies between the number of votes polled and votes counted in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. The Commission said it publishes details of electors, votes polled through electronic voting machines (EVMs), postal ballots and total votes cast.

SRINAGAR: As Ladakh’s administration Wednesday imposed a complete ban on protests and demonstrations within the municipal limits of Leh and Kargil, citing the municipal and hill council polls scheduled for Nov 23 and Dec 4, respectively, Ladakhi leaders, including Leh Apex Body (LAB) member and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk , appealed to President Droupadi Murmu, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah to intervene to defer the polls, citing harsh winter conditions and the likely exclusion of a large section of the electorate.“It is an SOS call from Ladakh to the President, the Prime Minister and the Union home minister. We are sending this message to the people of India also,” the joint appeal said.Earlier in the day, the office of the chief electoral officer issued an order stating that the model code of conduct has been enforced and will remain in force till the completion of the election process. The order said organising of political dharnas, protests, demonstrations, sit-ins, rallies or similar collective activities within the municipal limits of Leh and Kargil during the currency of the model code of conduct has the potential to intimidate voters, disturb public order, and vitiate the atmosphere for free and fair electionsFlanked by Ladakh MP Mohmad Haneefa, LAB co-chairman Chering Dorjay Lakrook and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) co-chairmen Asgar Ali Karbali and Sajjad Kargili, Wangchuk said the administration was forcing elections on people during the harsh winter, when temperatures in some parts of Ladakh fall below minus 30°C. “Ladakh is known as the world’s coldest inhabited place. The weather forecast for Dec indicates snowfall. How will elections be conducted in such conditions? Half of the population is outside Ladakh, while students are already studying in different cities. When Leh, Kargil and other areas are nearly empty, why are you holding elections?” he asked.“Indian democracy has a great tradition in Ladakh. Earlier, even two voters in Demchok were facilitated through helicopters to ensure their participation.So why is the administration ignoring half of the population now,” Wangchuk said. He appealed to the country’s leadership, including the opposition and people across India, to pay attention to Ladakh and oppose what he termed an arbitrary decision by the lieutenant-governor’s administration.Haneefa said he had met the Ladakh L-G and told him holding elections during winter would deprive a large number of people of their right to vote. He said despite it they issued the poll notification.Lakrook said holding elections during peak winter was unheard of in Ladakh. He said May or June would be more suitable time ensure maximum voter participation. Karbali accused the L-G of imposing its decisions on Ladakh’s people. He said the region has traditionally recorded around 90% voter turnout but the administration was scheduling elections at a time when nearly 30% of the population would be outside the Union Territory.Kargili alleged that the administration was making every effort to defame LAB and KDA and that holding elections in Dec was an infringement of people’s voting rights and a denial of adequate political representation.
Article Summary: Ladakh’s administration Wednesday imposed a complete ban on protests and demonstrations within the municipal limits of Leh and Kargil. Ladakhi leaders appealed to President Droupadi Murmu, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah to intervene to defer the polls.

Article Title: National Conference's twin troubles: Can Farooq Abdullah contain brewing revolt against Omar?
Article Text:
The Abdullahs are facing the challenge of keeping the National Conference united amid mounting dissent.

The show of unity

Farooq Abdullah dismisses reports of a split within the National Conference, asserting that the party remains united despite growing internal discontent.

The ideological rupture: Ruhullah's 'decree of freedom'

Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi accused the NC leadership of abandoning its promises on Kashmir's dignity and autonomy after the abrogation of Article 370.

The arithmetic ceiling

Omar Abdullah's Union Territory dilemma

CM Abdullah on statehood resolution.

Political space opening up beyond NC

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Two years after sweeping to power on a promise to reclaim Jammu and Kashmir ’s political identity and dignity, Omar Abdullah ’s government is confronting the limits of governing a Union Territory with constrained powers.What began as a historic return to power in October 2024 has increasingly turned into a political and administrative tightrope. While 89-year-old National Conference patron Farooq Abdullah has stepped in to contain simmering discontent among MLAs left out of the cabinet expansion, an ideological rupture has emerged with the exit of Srinagar MP Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi, who has accused the party leadership of abandoning its core promises.Caught between disgruntled legislators seeking a greater share in government and a prominent party voice questioning its political compromises, the National Conference faces a twin challenge. The party has accused the BJP of exploiting its internal divisions to engineer an ' Operation Lotus ' in Jammu and Kashmir. But is this an opposition attempt to destabilise the government, or does the turmoil point to a leadership crisis under Omar Abdullah?The gates of the Abdullahs' Gupkar residence in Srinagar opened to a familiar political spectacle last week as yet another party leadership put up a show of strength amid growing discontent within its ranks.Standing alongside 15 MLAs unhappy with the recent cabinet expansion, 89-year-old National Conference (NC) president Farooq Abdullah sought to project an image of an organisation firmly in control of its affairs."The baseless reports being spread that the National Conference is divided are completely false. This organisation is united, and those who think they can break this organisation should understand that it has never been broken and will never be broken," Farooq declared.He acknowledged that the legislators had genuine grievances and promised that some concerns would be addressed immediately, while others would be taken up gradually.But behind the show of unity, there's a bigger contradiction confronting Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah. The National Conference, which swept the 2024 assembly elections on the promise of reclaiming Kashmir's political identity, dignity and special status, is caught between the compromises of governing a Union Territory and the expectations of the constituency that brought it to power.The party is facing two distinct challenges. While a section of its MLAs is demanding a greater share in the government and a say in decision-making, one of its most prominent political voices, Srinagar MP Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi, has walked out accusing the leadership of abandoning the very promises on which it sought votes.The fragility of the NC's united front was exposed three days before Farooq met with the disgruntled legislators.On November 3, at a gathering in Behisht-e-Zehra Park in Budgam marking the 26th death anniversary of his assassinated father, Aga Syed Mehdi, Ruhullah announced his resignation from both the National Conference and the Lok Sabha.In an 80-minute address, the Srinagar MP launched a scathing attack on Farooq and Omar Abdullah, accusing the leadership of abandoning its promises on Article 370 , political prisoners and public relief.Describing his departure as a "decree of freedom", Ruhullah called the NC a "deceitful, corrupt organisation"."You told people that you were the guardians of their dignity. You said that if anyone touched that dignity, it would be like grabbing you by the collar. That dignity was buried on August 5, 2019. Tell me now, where is that dignity? Where is that autonomy?" he asked, targeting the party leadership.He accused the NC of seeking power on promises it had failed to fulfil and said he could no longer lend his name to what he described as political humiliation.On November 6, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla formally accepted his resignation, creating a vacancy in the Srinagar parliamentary constituency.Ruhullah's departure is more than an organisational setback for the NC. Elected to the Lok Sabha on the party's ticket in 2024, he had emerged as one of its most vocal faces on the question of Kashmir's political rights after the abrogation of Article 370 in August 2019.While Omar Abdullah has sought to pursue the restoration of statehood and special status through legislative and political channels, Ruhullah has demanded a more uncompromising approach. His exit gives him the opportunity to position himself as a voice of those who believe the NC has softened its stand after coming to power.He has hinted at launching a broader political movement rather than immediately forming a new party, saying he wants to bring together people committed to restoring the dignity and rights of Jammu and Kashmir.The NC, meanwhile, has questioned his own record, asking why he did not move a resolution or private member's bill in Parliament on special status or mobilise fellow MPs on the issue, despite having secured the support of more than 100 parliamentarians for an impeachment motion against an Allahabad High Court judge.The public exchange has exposed a larger ideological fault line: can the NC continue to claim ownership of the political struggle for Kashmir's rights while defending its record in government?While the ideological dissent has played out in public, the discontent within the legislative wing has centred on the distribution of power.The immediate trigger was the October 27 cabinet expansion, in which four new ministers were inducted, taking the council of ministers to its maximum permissible strength of nine.The restriction is rooted in Section 53 of the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019, which caps the council of ministers at 10% of the total membership of the Legislative Assembly. With 90 elected seats, the permissible strength is nine, including the chief minister.This creates a structural constraint for Omar Abdullah. Unlike a full-fledged state, where the constitutional ceiling for the council of ministers is 15% of the assembly's strength, Jammu and Kashmir's Union Territory framework leaves the CM with a smaller pool of ministerial positions to distribute.With all nine positions occupied, accommodating more aspirants would require dropping or replacing existing ministers.Several senior legislators, including six-time MLA Mubarak Gul, were reportedly unhappy at being left out. The discontent was not limited to ministerial berths. The legislators also raised concerns about administrative functioning, organisational decisions and what they described as the concentration of authority among a small group of leaders and advisers.A group of 18 aggrieved legislators had met a week before the Friday meeting. The subsequent gathering of 15 MLAs at Gupkar brought their grievances directly to Farooq and Omar Abdullah.The legislators reportedly sought a review of the cabinet, changes in the functioning of the CM's office and a mechanism to ensure that elected representatives have a greater say in government decisions.One of the legislators, Nazir Gurezi, sought to play down speculation about the emergence of a separate faction."A few days ago, we sat together at a place, and from there, social media hyped it up as if a separate faction had emerged from the National Conference. No separate faction or party has emerged," he said.Gurezi added that the legislators had placed their concerns before the CM and the party president, who had assured them that the issues would be addressed.For Omar Abdullah, however, the problem is not merely placating a group of unhappy MLAs. The cabinet expansion has exhausted the government's primary instrument of political accommodation. Any reshuffle could create fresh resentment among those who have already secured ministerial positions.Farooq's intervention may have prevented the discontent from turning into an open confrontation for now, but the leadership will have to find ways of accommodating senior legislators without triggering another round of dissatisfaction.The constraints facing Omar Abdullah go beyond cabinet arithmetic. They strike at the heart of the political contradiction of running an elected government in a Union Territory where the Lieutenant Governor and the Centre retain significant powers.Omar has repeatedly complained about the limits placed on his government, particularly in matters involving administration and the functioning of the bureaucracy.During the September 2026 assembly proceedings on a resolution seeking immediate restoration of full statehood, he revealed that the Law Secretary had written to the Speaker questioning whether the resolution should be discussed because the matter was sub judice. The chief secretary had also written to the Speaker.Omar, who also holds the law portfolio, expressed surprise at the communications."I am a law minister and I don't know that my law secretary is giving you an opinion. As a CM I don't know the chief secretary is writing to the Speaker against my resolution. I don't know on whose behalf it is being done," he said.He went on to question whether such a situation would arise in a full-fledged state."Would you think such a thing would happen in any State? This happens only in UT where a CM moves a resolution and the law secretary gives an opinion against it," he said.The episode illustrates the difficult position in which the chief minister finds himself. To deliver on everyday governance, including infrastructure, electricity, welfare schemes and administrative decisions, Omar has to work within the existing institutional arrangement. But the same arrangement limits his authority and has become a source of political frustration for his government.Every compromise with the Centre risks being interpreted by sections of the electorate as a dilution of the NC's political promises. Every confrontation, meanwhile, can further constrain the government's ability to function.The NC's August 19, 2024 manifesto had made restoration of Articles 370 and 35A a key promise. It also pledged to work towards restoration of statehood, repeal of the Public Safety Act and release of political prisoners.The party subsequently sought to demonstrate its commitment through the assembly. On November 6, 2024, the House passed a resolution seeking restoration of special status, a move Ruhullah had initially welcomed.But two years after the abrogation of Article 370, the Centre has given no indication of reversing its decision. Statehood, too, remains unresolved, while the reservation policy has become another source of friction between the government and sections of the electorate.The NC has defended its record on reservations, saying its cabinet sub-committee has initiated changes but that the decisions are awaiting action from the Centre and the Lieutenant Governor's administration.Farooq Abdullah, after Friday's meeting, reiterated that the party would continue its fight for statehood and Articles 370 and 35A, taking the struggle to its "logical conclusion".Ruhullah's exit could challenge the NC's claim to represent Kashmir's political aspirations. Having been elected on its ticket in 2024, he may now seek to occupy the political space he believes the party has vacated.The political implications will depend on whether Ruhullah can translate his criticism into an organised platform and attract support beyond his existing constituency. His resignation has already created a vacancy in Srinagar, and the eventual by-election could become an important test of the political space he hopes to occupy.The BJP has been quick to seize on the National Conference's internal troubles. On November 3, BJP national vice president Ram Madhav said Ruhullah's rally in Budgam had the blessings of "our people". The NC subsequently accused the BJP of attempting "Operation Lotus" in Kashmir, a charge the party has denied. For the BJP, the public friction within the ruling party offers an opportunity to question its cohesion and, more importantly, Omar Abdullah's leadership.The Congress, the NC's alliance partner, has taken a more cautious line. It has sought to play down the developments, attributing Ruhullah's departure to ideological differences while expressing confidence that the NC would resolve its internal disagreements.But the strains within its ally also pose a political concern for the Congress, given its investment in the governing arrangement.For the Abdullahs, however, the challenge is that the two crises have unfolded back-to-back on different fronts.Farooq Abdullah's show of unity at Gupkar may have helped contain the immediate optics of the MLAs' rebellion. It does little, however, to answer the larger questions raised by Ruhullah's exit.The next few months will answer whether Omar Abdullah can hold his flock together and retain the public's trust at the same time.
Article Summary: The National Conference is caught between the compromises of governing a Union Territory and the expectations of the constituency that brought it to power. The party is facing two distinct challenges. A section of its MLAs is demanding a greater share in the government and a say in decision-making. Srinagar MP Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi has walked out accusing the leadership of abandoning the very promises on which it sought votes.

3 CRPF men wounded as terrorists strike patrol in south Kashmir

SRINAGAR: A CRPF head constable and two constables were wounded when terrorists fired at a patrol in south Kashmir’s Akhran area of Kulgam district around 2pm Wednesday, ending a long lull in attacks on security forces in the valley. Constable Santosh Chandru, who suffered bullet wounds to his abdomen and spine, was airlifted to Army’s 92 Base Hospital in Srinagar in a critical condition. Constable Rakesh Dass and head constable Somveer Singh were stable.The attack on personnel of 46 CRPF battalion was the third major terrorist strike in Kashmir this year, but the first targeting security forces in a long time. The attackers escaped after the shooting.CCTV footage showed a CRPF trooper running for cover as gunfire erupted near a row of closed shops around 2.06pm. A colleague appeared from the left and moved towards the direction of gunfire. The first returned with his weapon and joined him. Another trooper in full combat gear was seen climbing onto a rooftop around 2.07pm. A minute later, a voice, apparently that of a wounded man outside the frame, could be heard saying: “Hamein goli lagi hai” (I am hit).A CRPF officer said the footage appeared genuine and was being examined. The attackers allegedly used a high-calibre weapon, possibly an AK-47. “It doesn’t look like pistol fire,” he said, declining to confirm whether they were riding a motorcycle.Army, CRPF and J&K police sealed the area and launched a manhunt. Security was heightened across Kashmir. Police described the strike as a sign of terrorists’ “growing frustration and desperation” in the face of heightened security alertness and area domination, and praised the personnel’s response.The attack happened while lieutenant governor Manoj Sinha was in Kulgam, attending a festival at Degree College, far from the site. CPM MLA MY Tarigami from Kulgam, who was with Sinha, said they learnt about the attack as the programme was drawing to a close. “We were celebrating our cultural heritage. There were poets and writers present and this happened. It is highly unfortunate,” he said, condemning terrorism.The strike came after Kashmir range IG Sujit Kumar said on Oct 5 that only one Kashmiri terrorist remained active in the valley, backed by a few foreign terrorists. Police identified him as Mohammad Lateef Bhat of Kulgam.
Article Summary: A CRPF head constable and two constables were wounded when terrorists fired at a patrol in south Kashmir. Constable Santosh Chandru was airlifted to Army’s 92 Base Hospital in Srinagar in a critical condition. The attack on personnel of 46 CRPF battalion was the third major terrorist strike in Kashmir this year.

Article Text:
Sukhbir Badal on Sonia Gandhi's memoir

NEW DELHI: Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) president Sukhbir Singh Badal on Wednesday criticised the Congress over Sonia Gandhi ’s remarks on Operation Blue Star , saying that she had given a “clean chit” to "the killers of thousands of innocent Sikhs."“Congress leaders in Punjab must break their silence over Sonia Gandhi’s clean chit to those responsible for the killing of thousands of innocent Sikhs in 1984,” the former Punjab deputy chief minister said in a post on X.Badal also claimed that Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, "Belonging: A Journey of Love," released in India on Tuesday, contained an “admission” that her husband, then Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi, had “purposely and personally” decided against deploying Army units in Delhi to protect the Sikh community.“This finally provides the clinching evidence of the Congress government’s patronage of the anti-Sikh massacre. The Congress government could send a Sikh general to lead Operation Blue Star at Sachkhand Sri Harmandir Sahib and Sri Akal Takht Sahib, but would not deploy Sikh Army personnel to protect innocent Sikhs in 1984?” he asked.The SAD chief was referring to retired lieutenant general Kuldeep Singh Brar, who commanded the Army's Operation Blue Star at the Golden Temple in Amritsar, Punjab.Badal further asked whether Punjab Congress leaders "endorse" Rajiv Gandhi's decision not to deploy the Army in Delhi."Do Punjab Congress leaders, including Sikh leaders, endorse this decision to leave innocent Sikhs at the mercy of marauding killers belonging to the Congress party and the government headed by Rajiv Gandhi? Will they ask Sonia Gandhi to explain why Rajiv Gandhi chose to stop the army deployment to save the lives of innocent Sikhs? Cowardly silence won’t do," he added.Anti-Sikh violence erupted across the country, particularly in Delhi, following the assassination of then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi by her Sikh bodyguards on October 31, 1984. The assassination came months after Operation Blue Star at the Golden Temple in June 1984. Indira Gandhi was succeeded as Prime Minister by her son, Rajiv Gandhi.In her memoir, Sonia Gandhi writes that her mother-in-law, Indira Gandhi, was “left with no choice” and “reluctantly” ordered the armed forces to launch Operation Blue Star.“Then intelligence reports informed Mrs Gandhi that the declaration of Khalistan as an independent state was imminent: Bhindranwale and his cohort planned to announce it and hoist its flag on the Har Mandir Sahib, the Golden Temple, on India's Independence Day, August 15,” she wrote.The former Congress president was referring to Jarnail Singh Bhindranwale, who led the movement for a separate Sikh homeland of Khalistan. Bhindranwale and his supporters had been based inside the Golden Temple complex since 1982."Indira Gandhi's own relationship with the Sikh community was a deep and strong one, but the problem was spiralling; she held meetings until late hours of the night, hardly ate her meals and looked disturbed for days ... A week or so later, an intelligence official brought to Mrs Gandhi a film with harrowing visuals of the aftermath: As my mother-in-law watched the slow-moving record, I could see her face wet with tears -- tears of pain and regret, I think: sorrow at the manner which the siege had ended, at the large number of lives lost. "Sonia Gandhi further wrote that Indira Gandhi had “flatly refused” to remove her Sikh bodyguards, a decision for which she ultimately “paid” with her life when two of them opened fire on her.
Article Summary: Sukhbir Singh Badal criticises Congress over Sonia Gandhi’s remarks on Operation Blue Star. Badal says Sonia Gandhi had given a “clean chit” to “the killers of thousands of innocent Sikhs’

Article Title: India must create, not just adopt inventions: Narayana Murthy calls for respect, better pay for teachers & researchers
Article Text:
Murthy said India had advanced in space, nuclear energy and vaccines but lagged in areas affecting everyday life.
